paths.description: Homepage and Wayback/library entry surface; covers global navigation, preferences, search affordance, performance and crawlability.
Movies collection listing representing browse/listing templates and async loading.
Public-domain query representing the primary search-results journey.
Big Buck Bunny media detail representing item metadata, playback, social/discoverability and media delivery.
Account signup representing forms, authentication choices, autofill, validation and trust.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt its main surfaces to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: With prefers-color-scheme: dark active, the computed probe reported color-scheme: normal, body background rgb(251,251,253), and text rgb(44,44,44), the same light palette.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map shared surface/text tokens through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), including shadow-root components.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible on many primary navigation links.
findings.evidence: The focus probe programmatically focused the first 30 controls; Wayback Machine, Texts, Video, Audio, Software, Images and several menu links computed outline-style:none, while Sign up and Log in had 0px outlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Use :focus-visible to provide a high-contrast, non-clipped focus indicator on every interactive element, including links inside shadow roots.

findings.summary: Primary browse, search, and playback journeys can stall or fail without useful recovery.
findings.evidence: After 8 seconds the Movies listing remained on an unlabeled spinner, search for “public domain” showed 0 results, and the item player displayed “failed to load (Error Code: 101104)” with no retry action.
findings.suggestedFix: Give all async surfaces bounded loading states, explicit error/empty distinctions, Retry controls, and a direct download/fallback path when playback fails.

findings.summary: Core content paints far too late on both the homepage and a representative item page.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 16.34s (performance 0.56) and item-page LCP 20.23s (performance 0.54); the item LCP image had a 15.81s discovery delay and no fetchpriority=high.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical request chains, server-render the first viewport, defer noncritical modules, and eagerly prioritize the actual LCP image with fetchpriority=high.

findings.summary: Homepage collection tiles and heading structure expose accessibility defects.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported heading-order failures and label-content-name-mismatch on collection tile links, where aria-label did not include the full visible text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sequential heading hierarchy and derive each tile’s accessible name from its visible label rather than overriding it with a divergent aria-label.

findings.summary: Item player controls have undersized touch targets.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured fullscreen, mute, and playback-speed controls at 15×12 CSS px with insufficient spacing, below its 24×24 minimum.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the interactive hit area and spacing of player controls to at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 for touch comfort.

findings.summary: Homepage and listing content is effectively unavailable without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Raw homepage/listing HTML is a bare <app-root> plus a “Javascript is required” message. Discoverability found only 33% shared words, no raw H1, and crawler screenshots contain no library content; the item template, by contrast, reached 96%.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful headings, search/browse links and representative collection content, then progressively enhance the interactive shell.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies leave avoidable XSS, MIME-sniffing, framing, and feature-control exposure.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found a CSP with default-src *, style-src unsafe-inline and no frame-ancestors, plus missing X-Content-Type-Options and Permissions-Policy. HSTS was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Tighten CSP allowlists, add frame-ancestors, send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and define a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Internationalisation support is partial and the tested item renders locale-sensitive data in fixed formats.
findings.evidence: The item showed ISO date 2009-12-09 and comma-grouped 457,169; stylesheet inspection found 395 physical left properties versus 6 logical inline properties, despite a global public audience.
findings.suggestedFix: Format user-facing dates and numbers with Intl and migrate layout rules to logical properties so RTL/localized layouts remain usable.

findings.summary: Signup fields omit or misuse autofill purpose tokens.
findings.evidence: The signup probe found email and screen-name inputs with empty autocomplete values, and the new account password field used autocomplete=current-password instead of new-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=email, username, and new-password on the corresponding signup controls; retain native required validation and visible labels.

findings.summary: The representative item’s LCP preview is not prioritized as a critical asset.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s LCP discovery insight reported priorityHinted:false for the video preview image; resource-load delay was 15.81s.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose the preview as an image discoverable in initial HTML and apply fetchpriority=high while avoiding lazy loading.

findings.summary: Heap retention grew substantially after repeated homepage scrolling.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary was 126,348 nodes / 7.36 MB self size; after ten bottom/top scroll cycles it was 166,653 nodes / 10.91 MB, a 32% node and 48% size increase. No Detached* constructor appeared, so the source of retention is not established.
findings.suggestedFix: Re-test infinite-scroll lifecycle in one instrumented session, cap retained tile data, unobserve discarded items, and release listeners/resources when cards leave the retained window.
